text:
Pittsburgh's season is starting to sound like an ending. The Penguins are winless in four (0-3-1) after a 6-2 home loss to Boston, outscored 18-11 in that stretch, and the headlines have moved past the standings: reports say Evgeni Malkin must submit a three-team trade list, Darren Dreger has linked him to Minnesota, another report has the Penguins fielding calls on Rickard Rakell, and the coverage of Sidney Crosby has turned to questions about how long he keeps going. "It is probably time for Dubas to brush up his sales pitches," Ryan Wilson of Hockey Hot Stove posted.

The frustrating part is that the play hasn't been terrible. Pittsburgh takes 52% of the expected goals at five on five and won the chance battle in three of its last five, but the power play creates just 0.46 expected goals a game, and Wilson's headline for it was one word: "Dreck." Bryan Rust is out until early December, so Tommy Novak has moved up beside Crosby and Rakell. Sergei Murashov starts over Arturs Silovs, and he has struggled (.871, 3.9 goals worse than expected).

The Kings come in loose after a 7-2 rout of San Jose in which Adrian Kempe scored three and passed Dustin Brown on a franchise list, and Kempe and Artemi Panarin combined for eight points. With Mats Zuccarello hurt, Panarin has slid into his spot beside Erik Haula and Alex Laferriere, and Corey Perry is up to 15:24 a night. Laferriere has gone eight games without a goal on 4.3 expected goals, which is the kind of drought that ends. Our sleeper is Quinton Byfield, 53% for a point with his ice time up and a line creating 3.97 expected goals per 60. Darcy Kuemper (.885) hasn't been much better than Murashov.

Our numbers call it close, 3.19 expected goals to 3.09 for Los Angeles. Both teams have 12 points; the Kings sit at 44% for the playoffs, the Penguins 19%. Another loss and the trade talk gets louder.
headline: The Penguins bring their trade rumors to Los Angeles

hunch.text: Eight games, 4.3 expected goals, no goals: Alex Laferriere is overdue, and a shaky Murashov is the right goalie to break it against.
